question: Which LLTO coating retained the most capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5C, how does it compare with the pristine NCM, and why did the 2 mol.% coating lower the rate capability?
rendered:
- [background] Liu et al. reported a lithium lanthanum titanate (LLTO) solid electrolyte coating on LiNi0.6Co0.2Mn0.2O2 (NCM), deposited using a novel coating approach which utilizes residual lithium on the cathode surface to form a coating layer as displayed in Fig. 7 (a) [100] .
- [result] The cycling performance of LLTO coated NCM also drastically improved when cycled at 0.5C as shown in Fig. 7 (e).
- [result] The pristine NCM only retained 56.6% of its initial discharge capacity after 200 cycles.
- [result] On the other hand, LLTO coated NCM retained about 85.5%, 57.2% and 86.2% for LLTO-0.5, LLTO-1 and LLTO-2 respectively.
- [interpretation] The prime reason for this improvement in capacity retention is the prevention of direct contact of cathode material with the electrolyte, thus suppressing the unwanted side reactions.
- [result] The 2 mol.% coating, however, decreased the rate capability, which may be due to the increase in the thickness of the coating layer, resulting in the suppression of electron transfer process during charge/discharge cycling.

The LLTO-2 coating retained the most capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5C, retaining 86.2% of its initial discharge capacity. This is compared with 56.6% for the pristine NCM. The 2 mol.% coating lowered the rate capability due to the increase in the thickness of the coating layer, which suppressed the electron transfer process during charge/discharge cycling.
